001: Are you going to attend the conference next Thursday?
Yes, I'm planning to go. I've been told there will be very interesting speakers.
I'm mostly interested in the talk about innovation. What about you?
Me too. We could go together and take the opportunity to make some contacts.
That sounds like a great idea to me. That way we can introduce each other to other people.
Perfect, so we'll meet on Thursday at the main entrance.
002: I don't really know how to start a conversation at these events.
The easiest thing is to ask someone about their job or their company.
And what if the person doesn't want to talk much?
You can always comment on something about the event or the talk you just saw.
You're right, that makes it more natural. Thanks for the advice.
You're welcome, you'll see that it will go well for you. Practice is what matters.
003: I met a director from a very important French company.
That's great! And what have you been talking about?
About possible collaborations between our companies. She asked me for my business card.
That's a big opportunity. You should write her an email first thing tomorrow.
Yes, I want to do it before I forget. Can you help me draft it?
Of course, we'll review it together and I'll give you my opinion.
004: How did it go for you at the industry trade fair on Friday?
Very well, although I was exhausted at the end of the day. I met a lot of people.
And did you get any really useful contact for the project?
Yes, I spoke with a supplier who offers exactly what we need.
I'm really glad to hear that. Are you planning to set up a meeting with him?
Yes, I wrote to him this morning to propose a video call next week.
005: I don't understand why having a good network of contacts is so important.
Because many opportunities come up through the people you know.
And isn't it enough to just do our job well?
Doing it well is essential, but knowing how to communicate it and meeting the right people is too.
I had never seen it that way. You make a very valid point.
Besides, a solid network helps you solve problems more quickly.
006: I've been invited to a business dinner next week.
And are you going to accept the invitation?
I think I should go, even though that kind of event makes me a little nervous.
It's normal to feel that way, but I'm sure you'll do great. Just be yourself.
And what do you recommend for making a good impression?
Listen carefully, show interest in others, and don't talk only about work.
007: I lost the contact information of a client I met at a conference.
Don't you have it saved on your phone or in your email?
No, I didn't think to exchange details before we said goodbye.
Try looking for him on the professional social network. A lot of people are registered there.
That's true, I hadn't thought of that. I'm going to look for him right now.
If you find him, send him a request with a brief and friendly message.
008: How do you manage to keep in touch with so many people?
I try to write to them every now and then, even if it's just to ask how they're doing.
And don't you find it tiresome to do that with everyone?
It's hard at first, but then it becomes a habit. Besides, you always learn something.
I see. I guess it's a matter of organization and consistency.
Exactly, and also of being sincere in the interest you show in others.
009: Last year I met an executive who now works for our competition.
And do you keep in touch with him?
Yes, we talk every now and then. He's a very interesting person.
Be careful, you wouldn't want it to seem like you're sharing confidential information.
Don't worry, we never talk about internal data from our companies.
I'm glad to hear that. Trust is important, but so is caution.
010: I've been asked to organize a gathering for alumni from my university.
And do you feel like taking on that responsibility?
I do, but I'm a little afraid of not being up to the task.
I think it's a fantastic opportunity to expand your network of contacts.
Yes, besides, it could be really useful for my professional career.
Without a doubt. Count on me to help you with the organization if you need it.
